guidance.statement: Suzlon aims to expand annual renewable energy sales to 10 GW, grow its orderbook to 15 GW, and scale its Asset Under Management to 70 GW by FY31.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 17-18% plus or minus 1-2% for FY27, with H2 operating leverage improving it.
Capex guidance of ₹700 Cr plus or minus ₹100 Cr remains intact, excluding DevCo investment.
Suzlon 2.0 ambition of 25% revenue CAGR over the next five years.
FY31 target of 10 GW RE sales, split 75:25 into 7,500 MW wind and the balance solar/BESS.
BESS target of 3.1 GW by FY31, with technology partnerships expected to close in the next couple of months.
DevCo investment capped at ₹500 Cr, revolving in nature, currently ₹200-300 Cr deployed.

industry: Industrials > Capital Goods > Electrical Equipment > Heavy Electrical Equipment

operating_notes.text: NCLT sanctioned Scheme of Arrangement for Reorganisation and Reclassification of Reserves effective 30th September 2024.
Suzlon secured a 195 MW wind order from Sunsure Energy in Bijapur district, Karnataka, taking total 3 MW platform sales to nearly 9 GW.
Highest-ever annual and quarter India deliveries at 2,456 MW and 830 MW respectively in FY26.
Suzlon announced 'Suzlon 2.0' strategy targeting 10 GW RE sales, 70 GW AUM, and 15 GW order book by FY31, with a new BESS manufacturing facility planned by 2027.
ASP rose to ₹6.3 Cr/MW in Q1FY27 from ₹5.6 Cr/MW in Q1FY26, aided by project mix, with EPC share up to 32% from 22%.
Order book is 6.1 GW, largely S144 3 MW series plus about 2 GW of retail/other demand; ~1 GW of orders won in the first four months of FY27, 60% from DevCo.
Foundry and forging revenue was ₹126 Cr with EBITDA of ₹22 Cr; AMS installed base is 16.1+ GW with machine availability above 95%.

timeline.summary: Suzlon Energy clarified on April 27, 2026, that it could not ascertain any mainstream media trigger for a material price movement.
NCLT Ahmedabad Bench sanctioned Suzlon Energy's scheme of arrangement for reorganisation and reclassification of reserves.
2026-05-12: Suzlon shareholders approved appointment of Girish Vanvari as Independent Director for five years
On May 22, 2026, Suzlon Energy announced a new 195 MW wind order from Sunsure Energy, taking its 3 MW platform sales to nearly 9 GW.
Suzlon Energy uploaded the audio recording for the Q4 FY26 earnings conference call held on May 25, 2026.
Vinod R.Tanti, Promoter of Suzlon Energy Limited, confirmed no promoter-group encumbrances on shares as of March 31, 2026, under SEBI’s Takeover Regulations.
SEBI WTM issued an order setting aside the earlier exoneration and imposed a ₹15.95 Cr penalty on Suzlon Energy concerning financial statements from FY 2013-14 to FY 2017-18.
Suzlon Energy reported a material price movement on 1st June 2026 without any corresponding mainstream media information.
On June 2, 2026, Suzlon Energy submitted the transcript of its Q4 FY26 earnings conference call.
Suzlon Energy announced its 'Suzlon 2.0' strategic ambition to reach 10 GW RE sales, 70 GW AUM, and a 15 GW order book by FY31.

2026-08-04: Suzlon filed the transcript of its Q1FY27 earnings call (held July 28, 2026), reporting 23% revenue growth to ₹3,819 Cr, flat EBITDA of ₹595 Cr, a 6.1 GW order book and ₹2,322 Cr net cash.

status_history.evidence: Order book at 6.1 GW with ~1 GW won in first four months of FY27; 506 MW delivered in Q1, highest-ever first quarter, but 10-20% of deliveries deferred.

watchlist.text: Commissioning (COD) catch-up from 1,257 MW erected pipeline

watchlist.response: Declined to quantify, saying only ₹40-50 Cr of upfront costs were in Q1 and it is a year-long journey, not a one-quarter story.
watchlist.text: Fixed costs in the WTG business stayed at Q4FY26 levels despite much lower volume; analysts pressed for the full-year fixed cost number.

watchlist.response: Gave a ₹40-50 Cr figure across subheads but did not provide the ex-cost margin.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked for the margin impact excluding Suzlon 2.0 upfront costs to assess the full year.

watchlist.response: Said pricing accounts for payable days and receivables are improving, but declined to predict the mix, calling it an evolving market.
watchlist.text: Receivable days for PSU versus C&I customers and whether the 85% PSU/C&I order book mix would persist.

watchlist.response: CFO declined to confirm the 4,500 to 7,500 MW number, saying only that capacity would be 'much higher'.
watchlist.text: Whether the 4.5 GW capacity would rise to 7.5 GW with the 5 MW machine, as suggested in a promoter interview.
